reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only supports that clustering dominates in Al0.1CrCoFeNi and that high-strain compression can induce ordering; it provides no data on heat-treatment-induced ordering, nor on electronic structure, phonons, or superconductivity. The key premises linking ordering to superconductivity are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Heat treatment at 500–700 °C can induce a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Enhanced short-range ordering modifies the local electronic density of states.
Enhanced short-range ordering alters the phonon dispersion.
Changes in electronic and phonon structure strengthen electron–phonon coupling.
Strengthened electron–phonon coupling elevates Tc and alters the superconducting gap.
